tasks.short: Build and revise technically valid product configurations against approved customer requirements.

steps.what: Translate approved requirements into configuration inputs.
Retrieve current components, specifications and compatibility constraints.
Select components and calculate compatibility, capacity and required options in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Discuss unsupported combinations and bespoke changes with design engineers.
Approve the configuration and any engineering exceptions for release.
Produce the configuration specification and component list for the proposal.

tasks.design: A configuration form in the {WORKFLOW} reuses approved requirement fields and loads versioned component data from the {ERP} and {DOCS}. A deterministic rules service on the {DATA_PLATFORM} calculates valid combinations and flags unsupported cases; engineering approval releases specifications and component lists into the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Compatibility knowledge sits across documents, calculations and experienced engineers. Building and maintaining a reliable rule set costs more than creating a configuration screen.
tasks.enabler_now: Rule engines and document generation are established technology. AI-assisted coding can reduce implementation effort, while structured requirement fields reduce rekeying.
tasks.still_hard: Codifying engineering constraints, validating rule interactions and handling bespoke designs remain substantial work.
tasks.human_edge: Judges whether a valid configuration is practical, maintainable and appropriate for the customer's operating conditions.

ambition.what: Customer option review comparing three technically valid configurations.

tasks.altitude: The sales engineer spends less time calculating combinations and preparing specifications, and more time comparing customer trade-offs. They can explore valid options within approved rules; engineering exception authority remains with the engineering lead.

reach.task: Convert an approved configuration into an accurate order.
reach.learn: Use configuration versions, component identifiers and release status to prevent order mismatches.

evidence.claim: Tacton CPQ provides rule-based product configuration and quoting.
Meyn reported single-machine quoting falling from two days to a week to under 15 minutes; this is a vendor-reported case.
The documented case supports deterministic configuration, but does not establish coverage or savings for another product portfolio.

assumptions: The baseline uses the {ERP}, technical documents and a configuration workbook; an established configurator would change the starting point.
The first release covers one repeatable product family with bounded options.
Approved requirements provide structured fields; ambiguous values return for clarification.
Only approved engineering rules enter the rules service.
Estimates include initial rule encoding; a large bespoke portfolio can require substantially more time.
An existing suitable configurator should be configured before building a new rules service.
unknowns: Does an existing configuration system already cover this product family?
How much of compatibility knowledge is documented and current?
Who owns engineering rule approval and change control?
Which calculations or configurations require specialist validation?
Can component identifiers and revisions be joined across the {ERP} and {DOCS}?
What access and employee consultation requirements apply under national rules?
research_questions: Which product family offers useful rule coverage with few bespoke exceptions?
Can historical configurations expose missing or contradictory constraints?
Which engineering calculations need independent validation before release?
new_work: Encode and approve compatibility rules and engineering changes.
Maintain regression examples for valid and invalid configurations.
Resolve unsupported cases and catalogue mismatches.
Review configuration releases and monitor stale rule versions.
Maintain generated document templates and integration mappings.
tasks.statement: Plan and modify product configurations to meet customer needs.

tasks.short: Discuss customer needs with customers and engineers, then agree system requirements.

steps.what: Review account context, existing equipment and previous technical discussions.
Prepare discovery questions and a requirements template.
Discuss operating needs, constraints and success measures with the customer.
Resolve technical questions and requirement conflicts with design engineers.
Write requirements, assumptions, acceptance measures and unresolved questions.

loop.input: Written discovery notes, engineering assessment and requirements schema.
loop.output: Requirements draft with units, source references, assumptions and unresolved conflicts.
loop.check: Validate required fields and units; trace each requirement to notes; sales engineer approves customer release.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction per meeting set; missing facts and conflicts return to the sales engineer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Written discussions express needs inconsistently and mix requirements with suggestions and assumptions.

steps.what: Confirm requirements or return corrections through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} assembles an account brief from the {CRM} and {DOCS}, then fills a standard discovery agenda. After human discussions, a bounded loop structures written notes into a requirements draft; reviewed customer release and explicit confirmation create versioned approved requirements in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Discovery is contextual, and notes mix needs with possible solutions. Templates help but do not remove transcription and reconciliation.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured forms handle known fields and missing-data prompts. A bounded extraction loop can draft structured requirements from written notes.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden operational constraints, conflicting stakeholders and measurable acceptance criteria require direct questioning and engineering judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Builds trust, notices hesitation and challenges requirements that would solve the wrong problem.

ambition.what: Customer requirement validation workshop with explicit acceptance measures.

tasks.altitude: The week retains customer and engineering conversations while preparation and documentation shrink. The sales engineer can lead a structured validation workshop; engineering and customer approval rights remain with their current owners.

reach.task: Run initial discovery before involving a sales engineer.
reach.learn: Distinguish stated preferences, operating constraints and measurable acceptance criteria.

evidence.claim: Structured agendas and requirements templates can be generated deterministically from known fields.
Verint Wrap Up Bot demonstrates converting call content into summaries and CRM records; it does not establish requirements accuracy.
GDPR applies to personal data in notes, including access, retention and processing arrangements.
In the Netherlands, employee-monitoring arrangements can require works council consent; consultation elsewhere depends on national rules.

assumptions: The baseline uses written notes; recording is not needed for this design.
Conversation remains the majority of the work, consistent with the supplied priors.
Customer confirmation covers the requirement baseline, not a guarantee of solution feasibility.
Estimates cover one discovery template and one team; consultation lead time can extend rollout.
unknowns: Who can confirm requirements for the customer?
Which notes and engineering documents may enter the processing environment?
What retention and confidentiality requirements apply?
Do national rules require employee consultation for the proposed workflow?
Which technical requirements need specialist approval?
research_questions: Can reviewers detect omitted constraints without rereading all notes?
Which requirement fields need strict units, ranges or controlled vocabulary?
new_work: Review extracted requirements and resolve conflicting notes.
Maintain discovery templates, field definitions and validation rules.
Track customer corrections and superseded requirement versions.
Manage access and retention for customer technical information.
tasks.statement: Confer with customers and engineers to assess equipment needs and to determine system requirements.

tasks.short: Work with the sales team to understand requirements and provide technical sales support.

steps.what: Review opportunity history and technical questions in the {CRM}.
Copy scattered account updates from the {EMAIL} and {CHAT} into opportunity notes.
Discuss requirements, buying concerns and technical uncertainties with the account manager.
Assemble relevant specifications, references and approved explanations from the {DOCS}.
Agree the sales approach, specialist involvement and next customer conversation.
Record agreed actions, owners and deadlines in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: Configure a shared opportunity view and a short action form in the {CRM}, so account updates are entered once and reminders follow agreed owners. A deterministic generator selects approved evidence from the {DOCS} using product and requirement tags, and flags unanswered questions. The engineer and account manager keep the discovery and sales-planning conversations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful context was spread across conversations and documents, with inconsistent opportunity records. Automating the conversation itself offered little value.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing record and reminder features can remove duplicate administration. AI-assisted coding makes a small evidence-pack generator practical without introducing an autonomous agent.
tasks.still_hard: Colleagues must keep the shared record useful. Ambiguous buying motives and disagreements about the sales approach still require direct discussion.
tasks.human_edge: Connecting technical uncertainty to the account manager's understanding of the buyer, politics and timing.

ambition.what: A scheduled technical qualification clinic for junior sales representatives.

tasks.altitude: The engineer spends less time reconstructing account history and more time coaching sales colleagues through technical qualification. Opportunity ownership and commercial approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Qualify technical fit before requesting a full demonstration or proposal.
reach.learn: Discovery questions, buying-process signals and when to escalate uncertainty.

evidence.claim: Shared opportunity records, filtered document retrieval and owner-based reminders can use configuration and deterministic code.
The supplied digest identifies advising and selling as human work; it supplies no direct case for replacing this collaboration.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates rather than measured outcomes.

assumptions: The team uses a shared opportunity record but also copies updates from messages.
Approved material can be tagged by product, requirement and version.
Action owners enter agreed fields once; free-form meeting transcription is outside the initial scope.
Access ranges include GDPR review and employee consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Whether duplicate message-to-record copying is material in this team.
Existing shared views, action forms and reminder capabilities.
Quality of evidence tags and willingness to maintain shared records.
Applicable access restrictions and employee-consultation requirements under national rules.
research_questions: Which minimal discovery fields improve technical handovers without burdening sales representatives?
When does exact tagged retrieval stop being adequate for technical support questions?
new_work: Maintain evidence tags and retire obsolete material.
Resolve unanswered technical questions.
Review adoption and remove unused fields or reminders.
Maintain access permissions and failed reminder queues.
tasks.statement: Collaborate with sales teams to understand customer requirements, to promote the sale of company products, and to provide sales support.

tasks.short: Win and renew orders, confirm terms, and coordinate delivery.

steps.what: Review account history, renewal dates, current pricing and delivery constraints.
Discuss requirements, handle objections and negotiate proposed terms with the customer.
Prepare a quotation using the configuration, price list and proposed terms.
Approve commercial exceptions and release the quotation to the customer.
Compare customer acceptance and purchase order against the released quotation.

loop.input: Customer acceptance and purchase order, plus the released quotation.
loop.output: Order fields with source passages; deterministic comparison produces discrepancies.
loop.check: Validate quantities, units, prices, currency and terms against the quotation; a person resolves differences.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per order; unreadable documents or unresolved differences remain manual.
loop.why_not_simpler: Customer documents and acceptance messages use inconsistent layouts and prose.

steps.what: Enter the accepted order and route it for fulfilment.
Confirm delivery arrangements with operations and the customer.

tasks.design: Connect {CRM}, {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} to assemble order briefs, populate quotation templates and transfer approved order data. A bounded extraction loop reads customer documents, while deterministic checks flag differences; people approve quotation release and delivery commitments through {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Customer terms arrived in varied documents, and account, pricing and delivery data crossed separate systems.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured quotation templates and faster integration development reduce copying. Bounded extraction makes document differences easier to review.
tasks.still_hard: Nonstandard engineering scope, delivery uncertainty and disputed contract terms need expert resolution.
tasks.human_edge: Earn agreement, negotiate trade-offs and recognise commitments the supplier cannot safely make.

ambition.what: A renewal readiness review covering technical fit and delivery feasibility before the renewal discussion.

tasks.altitude: The engineer spends less time assembling quotes and chasing order status, leaving more time for renewal discussions. Commercial approval and delivery commitment rights remain with their existing approvers.

reach.task: Resolve order discrepancies before fulfilment.
reach.learn: Order validation, delivery terms and the distinction between customer requests and accepted commitments.

evidence.claim: Tacton CPQ supports rule-based configuration and quoting.
Meyn reports single-machine quoting falling from two days to a week to under 15 minutes; this vendor case supports quotation preparation, not negotiation automation.
Validated order transfer and delivery notifications can use deterministic integrations and workflows.

assumptions: Shares cover active handling across the named roles, excluding customer and approval waiting time.
The first build covers standard orders with existing validated configurations and pricing rules.
Configured quotation generation is the preferred starting point; system support must be confirmed.
The coordination-heavy prior fits the paperwork, while negotiation remains human.
EU GDPR and EU AI Act obligations apply; access and employee consultation depend on national rules.
unknowns: Quotation-template and approval capabilities of the current systems.
Order interfaces, duplicate prevention and rollback options.
Frequency and types of customer term discrepancies.
Who may approve discounts, contractual exceptions and delivery promises.
Applicable access and employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: How reliably can extraction preserve units, revision numbers and referenced contractual terms?
Which order checks prevent the most fulfilment rework?
new_work: Review extracted order fields and commercial differences.
Handle failed transfers and changed delivery availability.
Maintain pricing, template and validation rules.
Monitor duplicate prevention and approval logs.
tasks.statement: Secure and renew orders and arrange delivery.

tasks.short: Develop and present technical proposals that meet customer requirements.

steps.what: Read customer documents and build a requirement matrix.

loop.input: Customer documents, including tables, attachments and submission instructions.
loop.output: Requirement matrix with source references, deadlines and unresolved ambiguities.
loop.check: Check attachment coverage, required fields and source references; engineer reviews omissions and ambiguity.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; unreadable or ambiguous sections return to the engineer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requirements appear in varied prose and tables; fixed parsing cannot reliably identify their meaning.

steps.what: Clarify priorities, constraints and acceptance criteria with the customer and account manager.
Check catalogue options, availability and costs in the {ERP}.
Confirm technical feasibility and resolve nonstandard commitments.
Write the proposal and requirement responses using approved technical material.

loop.input: Requirement matrix, approved design, calculated prices and approved answer library.
loop.output: Proposal draft with a cited response for each requirement and explicit gaps.
loop.check: Reconcile every requirement; validate prices deterministically; engineer verifies claims against cited sources.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per section; unsupported claims remain gaps for the engineer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Customer-specific explanations need prose synthesis; templates still handle standard sections and numerical fields.

steps.what: Approve pricing, delivery promises and commercial exceptions.
Present the solution and discuss customer objections.
Send the approved version and record submission in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: A requirement-matrix generator reads customer files from the {DOCS}; deterministic rules combine catalogue and cost data from the {ERP} into a proposed configuration. A bounded drafting loop assembles cited answers, while approval routing in the {WORKFLOW} controls technical and commercial commitments. After presentation, changed commitments return for approval before the approved version is sent through the {EMAIL} and logged in the {CRM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Product rules, past answers and pricing lived in separate places. Bespoke requirements still needed engineering judgement, making end-to-end automation unattractive.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building document generators, validators and connectors. Bounded extraction and drafting can handle prose while established rules handle configuration and calculation.
tasks.still_hard: Maintaining product constraints, proving unusual performance claims and agreeing customer acceptance criteria remain expensive. Confidential customer files require controlled access under GDPR.
tasks.human_edge: Discovering the customer's real constraint and making a credible technical commitment when the standard catalogue is insufficient.

ambition.what: A requirement-by-requirement technical fit assessment before a full proposal.

tasks.altitude: The engineer spends less time assembling documents and more time testing solution assumptions with customers. Technical sign-off, pricing and contractual decision rights remain with their designated roles.

reach.task: Choose which technically uncertain opportunities deserve engineering capacity.
reach.learn: Opportunity qualification, capacity trade-offs and commercial risk.

evidence.claim: Tacton provides rule-based configuration and quoting; this supports the configuration component, not general proposal judgement.
The vendor's Meyn case reports substantially faster single-machine quoting after configuration rules were introduced.
Source-linked RFP drafting is feasible with a bounded loop, but completeness and technical accuracy require validation.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates rather than measured outcomes.

assumptions: The baseline is a mixed catalogue and engineered-solution business, with the engineer coordinating specialist approval.
Build ranges cover one product family and a limited proposal format set.
Existing configuration features should be configured first when they cover the required rules.
Access estimates include GDPR review and employee consultation under national rules where applicable; they are not statutory timelines.
unknowns: How much of the product catalogue has explicit, maintained configuration rules.
Which technical claims and answers are approved for customer use.
Available interfaces, document quality, approval limits and actual proposal volumes.
Applicable employee-consultation requirements under national rules.

How accurately can source-coverage checks distinguish a supported answer from a merely related citation?
new_work: Review extracted requirements and unsupported answer gaps.
Maintain product constraints, approved answers and source expiry dates.
Handle connector failures and stale cost or availability data.
Revalidate changed proposals before external submission.
tasks.statement: Develop, present, or respond to proposals for specific customer requirements, including request for proposal responses and industry-specific solutions.

tasks.short: Sell technical products by matching customer requirements to feasible configurations, proposals and installation commitments.

steps.what: Review account history, technical questions and relevant product information.

loop.input: Permission-filtered account history, customer questions and current product documentation.
loop.output: A source-linked opportunity brief with known requirements and explicit gaps.
loop.check: Verify account identity, source permissions and document versions; the sales engineer checks material claims.
loop.stop: One brief and one correction pass per opportunity update; unsupported points remain questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Relevant facts are spread across free-text notes and technical documents; field retrieval alone misses context.

steps.what: Discover customer requirements, operating constraints and installation expectations.
Check configuration, installation prerequisites and operating limits against technical documents.
Prepare a priced proposal with scope, support and installation assumptions.
Explain trade-offs and negotiate scope, price and support commitments.
Approve final commercial terms and any exceptions.
Request and track customer acceptance through the {ESIGN}.
Record the accepted order and hand installation requirements to the delivery team.

tasks.design: A bounded reading loop prepares source-linked opportunity briefs from the {CRM} and {DOCS}. A configuration and quoting application in the {OTHER} applies explicit compatibility and pricing rules, fills proposals from the {ERP}, and routes technical and commercial approvals through the {WORKFLOW}. The {ESIGN} collects customer acceptance before a deterministic integration creates the order in the {ERP} and installation handoff in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Product rules were embedded in documents and expert knowledge, while pricing and order records lived elsewhere. Maintaining those rules and integrations was costly.
tasks.enabler_now: Rule-based configuration and quoting already have documented use. AI-assisted coding can reduce implementation effort, and bounded reading helps prepare for customer conversations without controlling the sale.
tasks.still_hard: Undocumented compatibility limits and custom installations require engineering judgement. Rule ownership, test coverage and data access remain substantial costs.
tasks.human_edge: The sales engineer uncovers unstated needs, explains consequential trade-offs and judges which commitments the delivery team can honour.

ambition.what: Reassess feasible configuration alternatives at each material customer requirement change.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from document assembly and duplicate entry toward discovery, trade-off discussions and installation planning. Within approved technical and commercial limits, the sales engineer can present alternatives earlier; exception approval rights stay with the existing approvers.

reach.task: Review opportunity quality and delivery risk before committing commercial terms.
reach.learn: Assess margin, implementation dependencies and evidence behind the proposed close date.

reach.task: Validate accepted orders before release to delivery.
reach.learn: Trace configuration versions, contract acceptance and installation prerequisites across records.

evidence.claim: Tacton CPQ supports rule-based product configuration and quoting.
Meyn reportedly reduced single-machine quoting from two days to a week to under 15 minutes. This vendor case does not establish savings for other firms.
Source-linked opportunity preparation and accepted-order integration are proposed patterns; their savings require local validation.
Automated acceptance tracking still requires an actual customer signature before order creation.

assumptions: The initial build covers one product family with explicit compatibility and pricing rules.
The {OTHER} category is a configuration and quoting application; configuring an existing capable application would be cheaper than building one.
Custom engineering decisions remain outside automatic configuration approval.
Only an unchanged approved proposal may be sent automatically for signature.
Order creation requires validated customer acceptance and matching configuration versions.
Shares describe active task effort across the sales engineer and sales manager, excluding customer waiting time.
GDPR applies to account and contact data; EU AI Act duties and consultation under national rules are assessed for the actual use.

How complete and current compatibility rules, price books and installation requirements are.
Which configurations need specialist engineering approval.
Which commercial exceptions require manager approval.
Whether the {ERP}, {CRM} and {ESIGN} expose reliable interfaces and version identifiers.
Whether national rules require consultation on the proposed use of employee activity records.

Can configuration rules reproduce accepted historical quotes and reject known invalid combinations?
Can signed terms be matched reliably to the configuration and price version before order creation?

Test rules after product and price changes.
Review source-linked briefs and generated proposals.
Resolve custom configurations and commercial exceptions.
Handle failed signatures, duplicate orders and integration errors.
tasks.statement: Sell products requiring extensive technical expertise and support for installation and use, such as material handling equipment, numerical-control machinery, or computer systems.

tasks.short: Investigate faults in installed equipment and agree the next action.

steps.what: Review equipment configuration, service history and reported symptoms.
Ask the operator when the fault occurs and what changed beforehand.
Inspect equipment and perform authorised tests using diagnostic instruments, the {OTHER} category.
Compare findings with fault guidance and evaluate possible causes.

loop.input: Observed findings and approved fault guidance for the equipment revision.
loop.output: Evidence table linking observations to documented causes, contradictions and missing tests.
loop.check: Check model and revision deterministically; the sales engineer verifies cited passages and applicability.
loop.stop: One extraction pass and one repair pass; absent evidence or contradictions return to manual investigation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed fault trees handle coded alarms, but narrative observations require text interpretation.

steps.what: Decide the likely cause and agree repair, further testing or specialist escalation.
Document the diagnosis and hand the action plan to the service team.

tasks.design: A read-only integration assembles equipment and service history from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and {HELPDESK}. Deterministic fault checks handle coded observations, while a bounded lookup in the {DOCS} prepares an evidence table for human diagnosis; approved structured findings populate the diagnostic report and service referral.
tasks.previous_blocker: Equipment histories were fragmented, and many faults depended on observations that were never captured consistently.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured test records and supported exports can automate preparation and reporting. Bounded text extraction can organise manual evidence without assuming a breakthrough in fault diagnosis.
tasks.still_hard: Intermittent faults, physical inspection, safe testing and causal judgement remain expensive and situational.
tasks.human_edge: Notice abnormal behaviour, test competing explanations and know when evidence is insufficient to resume operation.
tasks.altitude: The week contains less history retrieval and report assembly, but most diagnostic work remains. No new repair authority or equipment-release rights are granted.

reach.role: sales representative of technical and scientific products
reach.task: Collect useful fault details before handing a case to technical support.
reach.learn: Learn equipment identification, symptom timelines and the distinction between observations and diagnoses.

evidence.claim: History retrieval, deterministic fault checks and report generation can assist diagnosis without automating physical investigation.
The digest contains no documented case establishing autonomous diagnosis of installed equipment.

Time shares are estimates; physical and conversational investigation dominate, consistent with the supplied priors.
The first build covers one equipment family and reads records without controlling equipment.
Approved diagnostic findings are structured before report generation.
GDPR applies where service records identify people; customer equipment information also needs contractual access controls.
EU AI Act literacy duties apply, and employee consultation follows applicable national rules.
The access range includes consultation where required; customer site access can add elapsed delay.

Who authorises repair and return to operation?
Are equipment configurations and service histories complete?
Which fault codes have validated deterministic diagnostic rules?
Can customer equipment data be accessed remotely?
research_questions: Which recurring faults can be handled with approved fault trees alone?
Can evidence tables expose contradictory observations reliably?
How much preparation and reporting time is actually available to save?
new_work: Review evidence tables for wrong equipment revisions and unsupported links.
Maintain fault-code mappings and approved test procedures.
Handle missing service histories and inconsistent identifiers.
Validate report templates against actual diagnostic handoffs.
tasks.statement: Diagnose problems with installed equipment.

tasks.short: Recommend technical improvements and document their expected cost or production benefits.

steps.what: Discuss operating problems, constraints and success measures with the customer.
Collect customer operating figures and confirm missing values through {EMAIL}.
Calculate alternative costs, throughput and payback in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Assess feasibility and choose a recommendation with appropriate uncertainty and operating constraints.
Write the recommendation and supporting benefit calculation in the {DOCS}.
Approve customer use, explain the recommendation and agree validation or trial arrangements.

tasks.design: A form in the {WORKFLOW} captures baseline figures, units and assumptions; a calculator on the {DATA_PLATFORM} checks constraints and produces sensitivity tables from approved specifications in the {DOCS}. A deterministic report generator documents the selected recommendation, and the sales engineer approves customer use and explains its limitations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Customer baselines varied, calculators lived in individual workbooks and engineering assumptions were implicit. Software could calculate benefits but could not establish whether the inputs described the customer's operation.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes reusable calculators, unit checks and report templates cheaper to build. Existing configuration rules can supply feasible options without a model loop.
tasks.still_hard: Weak baseline measurements, integration constraints and uncertain operating conditions dominate the recommendation. Calculated benefits do not establish actual savings.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge implausible inputs, understand the customer's production risks and choose a defensible recommendation.

ambition.what: Post-installation savings reviews against the agreed operating baseline.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from workbook calculation and report assembly toward baseline validation and trials. The sales engineer gains no authority to guarantee savings or approve customer investment.

reach.task: Evaluate the commercial strength of a technically justified proposal.
reach.learn: Learn contribution margin, investment hurdles and how uncertainty affects negotiation.

evidence.claim: Tacton CPQ supports rule-based configuration and quoting; this supports feasible option generation, not verified savings.
Meyn's documented vendor case reports faster rule-based quoting; it does not establish recommendation accuracy.
Deterministic cost and throughput calculations can generate qualified benefit reports from structured inputs.

assumptions: The pilot covers one equipment or material family with documented calculation methods.
A configurable calculator is used where available; custom code fills only missing calculations and checks.
Time shares are illustrative; analytical work is higher than the supplied spreadsheet prior for this example.
The customer technical lead supplies operating data; the sales engineer checks whether it is usable.
GDPR applies to personal data; relevant EU AI Act obligations and national rules must be assessed.
Build estimates exclude creating new engineering models or conducting physical trials.

Maintain units, prices, constraints and assumption defaults.
Review out-of-range inputs and unsupported operating conditions.
Collect and compare post-installation measurements if the new service is adopted.
tasks.statement: Recommend improved materials or machinery to customers, documenting how such changes will lower costs or increase production.

tasks.short: Prepare and deliver technical presentations tailored to customers and prospects.

steps.what: Clarify the audience, technical questions and desired outcome with the account manager.
Find approved specifications, diagrams and reference material in the {DOCS}.
Adapt slides and examples to the customer's needs in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Presentation brief, approved source pack and fixed slide template.
loop.output: Presentation draft with source references beside technical claims.
loop.check: Validate required sections and references; sales engineer checks claims, suitability and confidential content.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unsupported sections return to the sales engineer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates assemble standard slides, but customer-specific explanations require writing from free-text requirements.

steps.what: Check technical claims, choose examples and approve the presentation for customer use.
Present, demonstrate and answer customer questions during a call.
Record customer questions and agreed next steps in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: A reusable presentation builder on the {DATA_PLATFORM} selects approved material from the {DOCS}, fills standard slides and uses one bounded writing loop for customer-specific explanations. The sales engineer approves the presentation before customer use, delivers it personally and captures next steps through a short form in the {CRM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Approved content was scattered, and tailoring explanations took skilled writing. Maintaining a custom slide builder rarely justified its cost.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the effort to build template assembly and source checks. A bounded writing loop can draft the variable narrative from an approved source pack.
tasks.still_hard: Specifications change, demonstrations fail and customers ask questions outside the brief. Technical credibility and confidential reference permissions still require judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Read the audience, expose misunderstandings and explain trade-offs without making unsupported promises.

ambition.what: Customer-specific technical briefing packs for attendees to share internally.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less slide assembly and more customer preparation and discussion. The sales engineer gains no commercial approval rights; they can select approved examples and demonstration routes within their existing remit.

reach.task: Qualify the business problem before requesting a technical presentation.
reach.learn: Learn discovery questions, buying roles and the difference between interest and a funded requirement.

evidence.claim: Template assembly and source-linked drafting can reduce preparation effort while delivery remains human.
The time split gives customer discussion the largest share; preparation remains a separate automation opportunity.

assumptions: This describes a typical technical sales team in a European company with 200 to 2,000 staff.
Time shares are illustrative priors, not measured savings; this example has more preparation than the supplied means prior.
A pilot covers one product family, one presentation template and an approved content library.
Build ranges are working-day estimates, with access and consultation elapsed time potentially longer.
Customer data processing must meet GDPR; EU AI Act obligations apply where relevant.
The pilot uses written notes rather than call recording.
unknowns: Where approved specifications and reusable slides are stored.
Who may approve technical claims and customer references.
Whether the {DOCS} and {CRM} allow supported access or approved exports.
Which national rules and employee consultation requirements apply.

Which presentation formats support reliable automated assembly and source references?
new_work: Review drafted explanations and source references.
Retire obsolete slides and specifications.
Maintain templates, access permissions and integration checks.
Handle missing sources and customer-specific confidentiality restrictions.
tasks.statement: Prepare and deliver technical presentations that explain products or services to customers and prospective customers.

tasks.short: Help customers and colleagues use, operate and maintain equipment.

steps.what: Log the support request and link the customer and equipment record.
Ask the requester about symptoms, operating conditions and previous actions.
Find applicable operating instructions, maintenance guidance and previous support cases.

loop.input: Support context and approved manuals filtered by equipment model and revision.
loop.output: Relevant passages, source references and explicit information gaps.
loop.check: Verify source existence, equipment applicability and revision; retain original warnings alongside passages.
loop.stop: One retrieval and one extraction pass; missing or conflicting guidance returns an evidence gap.
loop.why_not_simpler: Metadata filters identify manuals, but varied symptom descriptions need a bounded text-matching step.

steps.what: Explain suitable actions and check the requester understands their limits.
Arrange specialist support or a service visit when advice is insufficient.
Record advice, actions and follow-up commitments in the support ticket.

loop.input: Sales engineer's notes, support advice and service referral.
loop.output: Ticket update separating advice, completed actions and future commitments.
loop.check: The sales engineer checks action status, equipment identity and commitments before saving.

Prepare a technical opportunity brief for the account representative.

loop.input: Qualified opportunity, account brief and approved product passages.
loop.output: Technical opportunity brief separating supported benefits, assumptions and open questions.
loop.check: Product claims cite approved passages; commercial facts match account fields; sales engineer approves release.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction per opportunity; unresolved claims become explicit questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: The brief must connect varied customer circumstances to technical benefits expressed in prose.

steps.what: Agree technical next steps and responsibilities with the account representative.
Record the opportunity, owners and follow-up dates in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: Join account, order and installed-product data from the {CRM} and {ERP}, then show explicit eligibility and compatibility filters in the {BI}. A bounded loop drafts technical briefs from reviewed opportunities and approved material in the {DOCS}; configured {CRM} workflows record agreed actions and reminders.
tasks.previous_blocker: Installed-product records and account history are fragmented. Technical suitability and relationship knowledge are difficult to encode.
tasks.enabler_now: Small integrations can assemble account briefs, while explicit rules expose obvious candidates. Grounded drafting reduces brief preparation without deciding customer intent.
tasks.still_hard: Buying appetite, channel conflict, incomplete installation records and commercial timing need people.
tasks.human_edge: Understands whether a technically plausible opportunity is welcome, credible and worth pursuing.

ambition.what: Technical expansion reviews for smaller reseller accounts.

tasks.altitude: The sales engineer spends less time assembling account facts and can support smaller accounts. They recommend technical pursuit priorities; account ownership and commercial decision rights stay with the existing roles.

reach.task: Qualify an expansion opportunity before requesting engineering support.
reach.learn: Use installed-product evidence, buying triggers and explicit technical disqualifiers.

evidence.claim: Account joins, explicit opportunity filters and follow-up workflows are established deterministic patterns.
The digest supports approved-library drafting as a bounded-loop pattern, but provides no resale-specific product case.
Personal contact data requires a GDPR lawful basis and appropriate access controls.

assumptions: Resale means repeat sales or sales through resellers, rather than disposal of used equipment.
Relationship work remains the largest part of this task.
The initial filters use explicit facts, not inferred purchase propensity.
Estimates cover one sales team and one product family.

Are installed products linked reliably to accounts and orders?
Which channel restrictions and account ownership rules apply?
Which contact-data purposes and access rights are authorised?
Is employee consultation required under applicable national rules?

Do smaller accounts have enough reliable data for useful expansion reviews?
new_work: Resolve account and installed-product mismatches.
Review briefs and reject weak opportunity suggestions.
Maintain compatibility filters, ownership rules and connector mappings.
Track whether accepted opportunities progress.
tasks.statement: Identify resale opportunities and support them to achieve sales plans.

tasks.short: Keep account activity and transaction records current, and produce sales reports.

steps.what: Collect correspondence, meeting notes and transaction documents for each account.
Enter account links, transaction references and activity dates in the {CRM}.
Summarize discussions, customer questions and agreed next steps in the {CRM}.

loop.input: Selected written notes and account correspondence, with source identifiers.
loop.output: Draft activity summary, explicit commitments, dates and proposed follow-up tasks.
loop.check: Require source references; flag ambiguous owners and dates; sales engineer approves before save.
loop.stop: One draft per activity and one correction pass; unresolved ambiguity returns to the sales engineer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text discussions express commitments inconsistently; field mappings cannot reliably recover their meaning.

steps.what: Check missing references, duplicates and mismatches against source records.
Generate account and transaction reports from the {CRM}.
Send account reports and unresolved exceptions to internal colleagues through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Supported synchronization between the {CRM}, {ERP}, {EMAIL} and {DOCS} links source records using stable account and transaction identifiers, with custom deterministic mappings only where needed. A bounded extraction loop drafts activity notes for approval before saving; configured reports and notifications route exceptions to the sales operations team while financial records remain authoritative in the {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Systems lacked consistent account links, and notes were mixed with structured transaction data. Automating all entries together risked turning an inferred commitment into an official record.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing synchronization and reporting features handle structured fields. AI-assisted coding makes missing mappings cheaper, while bounded extraction handles selected free text with source references.
tasks.still_hard: Identity mismatches, disputed commitments and retention requirements remain. Access to correspondence must be narrow, and synchronization must preserve source ownership.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize when a note misstates a promise, an account relationship or a commercially sensitive issue.

ambition.what: Weekly review of unresolved technical commitments before account handovers.

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer repeated entries and more focused review of commitments and exceptions. The sales engineer gains no rights to change financial transactions or make additional customer commitments.

reach.task: Resolve order-reference and customer-account mismatches.
reach.learn: Learn order status definitions, master-data ownership and the boundary between sales notes and financial records.

evidence.claim: Verint Wrap Up Bot writes call transcripts and summaries to customer records.
The AXA Health vendor case reports reduced after-call handling time in a service desk; transfer to sales engineering is unproven.
Structured transaction references can be synchronized deterministically with identity checks and duplicate prevention.
GDPR requires an appropriate basis, controlled access and retention for personal correspondence used in activity records.

assumptions: The sales engineer records account activity and transaction references, rather than posting accounting entries.
Time shares are illustrative; routine record entry is treated as reversible, unlike changes to binding transaction records.
Written notes and selected correspondence are sufficient for the pilot; call recording is excluded.
Existing supported synchronization is configured before custom integration is built.
The pilot covers one team and a limited set of account activity fields.
GDPR and relevant EU AI Act obligations apply; employee consultation and monitoring requirements depend on national rules.
Adding recording later would require a separate legal, access and consultation assessment.
unknowns: Whether the {CRM} already synchronizes correspondence and transactions.
Which system owns customer, supplier and order identifiers.
Whether notes contain restricted personal data or confidential customer material.
Who may correct records and resolve disputed commitments.
What retention periods, access rules and national consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: How accurately can bounded extraction distinguish explicit commitments from tentative discussion?
Which synchronization patterns best preserve provenance and prevent duplicate activity records?
new_work: Approve extracted summaries and commitments before saving.
Resolve identity mismatches and ambiguous transaction links.
Monitor synchronization failures and duplicate prevention.
Maintain field mappings, extraction checks and retention rules.
Review report permissions when account responsibilities change.
tasks.statement: Document account activities, generate reports, and keep records of business transactions with customers and suppliers.

tasks.short: Train sales team members to explain and apply technologies in customer situations.

steps.what: Review customer questions and recurring technical gaps.

loop.input: Permission-filtered customer questions, opportunity notes and training feedback.
loop.output: Grouped application questions with references and suggested learning gaps.
loop.check: Check source permissions and references; the sales engineer reviews grouping and removes unsupported inferences.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one correction pass per training batch; unclear items remain unclassified.
loop.why_not_simpler: Questions use inconsistent free text and often describe the same application problem in different words.

steps.what: Choose learning objectives and realistic customer scenarios.
Prepare examples, exercises and application guidance.

loop.input: Approved session brief, current product documentation and training template.
loop.output: Draft exercises and application guidance with source-linked technical claims.
loop.check: Validate required sections and source versions; the sales engineer checks examples, operating limits and answer keys.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per session; unsupported examples are removed or written manually.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates supply structure, but adapting explanations and exercises to customer scenarios requires language generation.

steps.what: Run a practical workshop and discuss customer application choices.
Assess application reasoning and give individual coaching.
Publish approved resources and record session completion in the {LMS}.

tasks.design: A bounded loop groups permission-filtered questions from the {CRM} and {EMAIL}; the sales engineer selects the learning objectives. A second bounded loop drafts source-linked exercises in the {DOCS}, while the {LMS} distributes approved resources and records completion after human-led practice and coaching.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful customer examples were scattered, and preparing good exercises required repeated writing. Workshop delivery and coaching could not be reduced to a fixed script.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded classification and drafting can reuse approved technical sources. Configured distribution and inexpensive integrations remove repetitive publishing work.
tasks.still_hard: Good teaching depends on spotting misunderstanding and adjusting explanations. Customer examples need confidentiality checks, and technical answer keys need expert review.
tasks.human_edge: The trainer notices weak reasoning, creates trust for questions and connects abstract technology to a customer's actual operating context.

ambition.what: Application workshops for newly hired sales representatives before their first technical customer meeting.

tasks.altitude: Preparation takes less of the week, leaving more time for practice and individual coaching. The sales engineer gains room to propose an onboarding workshop; formal certification rights do not change.

reach.task: Coach representatives before technical customer meetings.
reach.learn: Use scenario-based observation and constructive feedback to identify capability gaps.

evidence.claim: Bounded drafting from approved technical sources can support training preparation, subject to expert checking.
The digest provides no documented case establishing savings for sales-engineering training.
The EU AI Act distinguishes employment-related AI uses; classification depends on intended purpose.

assumptions: The initial scope covers one application family and existing approved training sources.
Practice assessment remains human coaching; generated materials do not make employment decisions.
Customer examples are minimised and permission-filtered before model processing.
Access and consultation estimates include GDPR review of customer and learner data and national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Whether customer examples may be reused for internal training.
Whether the {CRM} records application questions consistently.
Who approves technical training content and maintains answer keys.
Whether national rules require consultation on the use of employee learning records.
research_questions: Do generated exercises expose the misconceptions seen in customer meetings?
How much expert correction is needed before materials are suitable for new representatives?
new_work: Review generated exercises and technical answer keys.
Remove identifying customer details from examples.
Refresh materials after product changes.
Maintain source permissions and resolve unanswered questions.
tasks.statement: Train team members in the customer applications of technologies.

tasks.short: Maintain sales forecasts from opportunity records, order data and sales judgement.

steps.what: Export opportunity and order data from the {CRM} and {ERP}.
Chase missing values, close dates and technical milestones through {EMAIL}.
Reconcile pipeline and orders, checking duplicates, currencies and statuses in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Calculate forecast totals and changes by period in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Review technical risks and approve forecast assumptions and overrides.
Format the approved report and distribute it through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: A scheduled feed on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reads the {CRM} and {ERP}, replaces hand-created exports and reconciles records using identifiers, currencies and status rules. Existing forecast features or the {BI} produce draft totals and exception views; the {WORKFLOW} requests missing fields and distributes a dated snapshot after sales manager approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different identifiers, stale opportunity fields and repeated workbook adjustments made consolidation fragile. Forecast software could aggregate numbers but could not settle contested deal timing.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forecast and dashboard features cover much of the task. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort to build the remaining mappings, checks and snapshot process.
tasks.still_hard: Sales judgement, technical dependencies and strategic deal optimism remain uncertain. Reliable totals do not make close dates reliable.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish evidence of technical readiness from confidence expressed by the selling team.

ambition.what: Weekly escalation of technical risks that threaten forecast close dates.

tasks.altitude: The sales engineer spends less time assembling reports and more time resolving technical risk signals with account managers. They can recommend escalations more often; the sales manager retains forecast approval and resource decisions.

reach.task: Run a forecast review focused on decisions and deal risks.
reach.learn: Learn forecast categories, historical calibration and how to distinguish a factual correction from an override.

evidence.claim: Structured pipeline aggregation, validation and reporting generally need configuration and deterministic integration.
A forecast approval decision remains human when deal timing depends on commercial and technical judgement.

assumptions: The company maintains opportunity records in the {CRM} and booked orders in the {ERP}.
The sales engineer contributes technical risk information; the sales manager approves the consolidated forecast.
Time shares include immediate handoffs and are illustrative rather than a measured owner-only time study.
Automated reminders request corrections; account managers still supply the missing facts.
The pilot covers one pipeline, agreed forecast categories and supported read access.
GDPR applies to identifiable pipeline data; employee monitoring use would require separate assessment under EU law and national rules.
No model loop or new predictive forecasting model is required.
unknowns: Which forecast features are already licensed and configured.
Whether opportunities and orders share stable identifiers.
Who maintains exchange rates, stage definitions and technical milestones.
Which recipients may see customer-level forecasts.
Whether consultation is required for the proposed visibility into employee activities.
research_questions: Which simple historical calibration methods improve this type of pipeline forecast?
What reconciliation patterns best handle partial orders and opportunities split across reporting periods?
new_work: Resolve unmatched orders, duplicate opportunities and stale fields.
Maintain mapping tables, forecast definitions and exchange-rate sources.
Review material variances and record override reasons.
Monitor feed failures and reconcile snapshots against source totals.
tasks.statement: Maintain sales forecasting reports.

tasks.short: Attend industry events to demonstrate products, build relationships and learn.

steps.what: Review the event programme and prepare technical talking points.

loop.input: Event programme, approved product material and target criteria.
loop.output: Session suggestions and technical talking points with source references.
loop.check: Product claims must trace to approved material; the engineer checks relevance and demonstration limits.
loop.stop: One brief and one repair per event; unsupported topics remain questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Session descriptions and their relevance to technical needs are expressed in prose.

steps.what: Arrange attendance and meetings with relevant contacts.
Attend sessions, demonstrate products and discuss needs with attendees.
Write up event learning and add relevant contacts to account records.

loop.input: The engineer's event notes and contact details.
loop.output: Draft contact fields, learning points and explicit follow-up commitments.
loop.check: Trace commitments to notes, check account matches and exclude unsupported personal inferences.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per note batch; ambiguous contacts or commitments stay manual.
loop.why_not_simpler: Handwritten or free-text notes mix observations, names and promises.

steps.what: Assign follow-up actions and share technical learning with the sales team.

tasks.design: A bounded loop prepares an event brief from approved {DOCS} material, and configured {CALENDAR} features assist meeting arrangements. After attendance, a second bounded loop turns notes into reviewed {CRM} records and a learning summary in {DOCS}; configured follow-up rules assign internal tasks.
tasks.previous_blocker: The main value comes from live attendance. Preparation and follow-up were too fragmented to justify a separate tool.
tasks.enabler_now: Small drafting and note-extraction features can be attached to existing records and scheduling workflows.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected conversations, live demonstrations and interpreting weak industry signals remain situational.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, adapt a demonstration and notice what people hesitate to say.
tasks.altitude: The week changes modestly: event preparation and write-up take less time, while attendance remains central. Decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Prepare a technically accurate event demonstration.
reach.learn: Demonstration safety, approved product claims and how to adapt explanations to different audiences.

evidence.claim: Configured scheduling and follow-up rules can reduce event administration.
Bounded drafting and note extraction can assist event paperwork; no direct event-attendance case appears in the digest.
Collecting event contact details does not itself establish permission for every later marketing use under GDPR.

assumptions: Shares represent active event work, excluding travel.
Most time remains live attendance, consistent with the strong human-work prior.
The proposed note flow uses notes the engineer supplies and does not require conversation recording.
Savings concern preparation and paperwork, not replacing event participation.
EU GDPR and EU AI Act obligations apply; national rules determine any employee consultation.

Quality and format of event notes.
Rules for retaining and using event contact details.
Who owns follow-up after an event.
Applicable access and employee consultation requirements.

Which event observations are useful enough to retain in a shared learning summary?

Correct ambiguous account matches.
Maintain approved technical material.
Remove stale event contacts and monitor overdue follow-up.

tasks.short: Report prospective customers’ credit ratings and relevant payment history to the sales manager.

steps.what: Confirm the prospect’s legal entity and identify the reporting request.
Retrieve the credit report from an external credit information service.
Check existing payment history and explain discrepancies with the credit report.
Copy the rating, source date, payment context and warnings into a report.
Assess commercial context, qualify uncertainty and approve the summary for reporting.
Send the approved summary to the sales manager and record the report.

tasks.design: A deterministic integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} matches the prospect in the {CRM} to licensed credit information from the {OTHER} credit information service and payment history in the {ERP}. A configured {WORKFLOW} fills a report in the {DOCS}, routes discrepancies to the finance team, and sends the sales engineer’s approved summary through the {EMAIL}, recording delivery in the {CRM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Entity matching, licensed data access and finance context sit across separate systems. Bespoke integrations and report templates were often uneconomic for an infrequent task.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building connectors, validation rules and templates. Structured credit data and stable identifiers make a model loop unnecessary where those inputs are available.
tasks.still_hard: Credit information can be stale or conflict with internal experience. Licensing, entity ambiguity and bespoke interfaces can dominate cost; automation does not establish creditworthiness.
tasks.human_edge: The sales engineer explains the commercial context and uncertainty. The finance team interprets payment exceptions; authorised managers retain credit and trading decisions.

ambition.what: Weekly credit-deterioration review for active corporate prospects.

tasks.altitude: The sales engineer spends less time retrieving reports and copying facts, and more time discussing uncertain prospects with finance. No additional authority to approve credit or change trading terms is gained.

reach.task: Prioritise opportunities for a credit-risk discussion before committing further sales effort.
reach.learn: Understand rating freshness, exposure thresholds and when finance must decide.

reach.task: Check that an incoming order has the required credit clearance.
reach.learn: Understand legal-entity matching, clearance status and escalation routes.

evidence.claim: Structured identifiers, credit fields and payment records can support deterministic matching and templated reporting.
Conflicting financial information and commercial context still require human assessment.
GDPR applies where records contain personal data; employee consultation requirements depend on national rules and implementation.

assumptions: This is an illustrative workflow for a mid-size European company, not an observed customer process.
The scope is reporting on corporate prospects, rather than assessing consumer credit or sole traders.
The company already licenses structured credit information with permitted automated access.
Payment history may be absent for a new prospect; absence is reported explicitly.
Time shares represent participant effort per report. Remaining percentages and build ranges are planning estimates.
Access estimates include permissions and a consultation assessment; required consultation under national rules may extend elapsed time.
Existing software supports report approval and internal notification.
unknowns: Which role currently retrieves credit reports and how often reports are requested.
Whether licensed credit data permits automated retrieval, internal redistribution and retention.
Whether legal-entity identifiers are complete and consistent across systems.
Which finance checks, approval thresholds and escalation routes apply.
Whether existing integrations, report templates and approval features are available.
Which national rules and employee consultation arrangements apply.
Actual task effort, exception rates and recurring data charges.
research_questions: Which minimum fields let a sales manager understand the rating without recreating finance’s assessment?
Can the current credit service and internal systems support the workflow through configuration alone?
Does a weekly deterioration review change a useful decision often enough to justify recurring data costs?

Review payment discrepancies and commercial qualifications.
Maintain field mappings, report templates and escalation thresholds.
Monitor connector failures, licence limits and access permissions.
Sample generated summaries for source accuracy and correct recipients.
